scope: Reference-building pass, selected lyric concordance; not exhaustive track-by-track interpretation.

evidence_classes.D: direct name, title, distinctive phrase or cluster

references.group: A • Love, memory, and divergent selves
references.title: Sword Art Online — a relationship that survives changing worlds
references.canon:
Use arc names rather than assuming every service numbers four seasons identically. Aincrad makes Kirito and Asuna comrades, lovers, and a virtual household with Yui; their cabin gives survival a domestic purpose. Fairy Dance separates them after the game clears: Asuna is imprisoned in ALfheim’s World Tree, while Kirito searches from outside. Her own escape efforts matter, not just his rescue. SAO II moves through Phantom Bullet, Calibur, and Mother’s Rosario. In the last, Asuna’s friendship with the terminally ill Yuuki and the Sleeping Knights turns a boss victory into a memorial and helps Asuna find her own voice. [SAO1–SAO3]

Alicization places Kirito in Underworld with Eugeo and Alice. The Gigas Cedar is a generations-long assigned task; cutting it opens a route away from inherited limits. Alice’s removal and the ascent of the Central Cathedral expose an order maintained partly through memory manipulation. War of Underworld makes artificial people’s lives ethically consequential. At the accelerated-time deadline, Asuna deliberately remains with Kirito rather than leaving him alone for the projected two hundred years. [SAO4–SAO6]
references.load: The relationship is reciprocal across changing distributions of power: fighter beside fighter, rescuer and imprisoned partner, Asuna as Yuuki’s student, Asuna as the one who comes after Kirito. Love includes cooking, companionship, illness, grief, persistence, and the right to decide—not merely an unlimited willingness to suffer.
anchors: A named Asuna frame loads several fictional relationships together.
Mother’s Rosario, seasons, tree, tower, and a trusting leap.
Season Three, chopping a tree, and someone coming after the speaker.
Memory removal described as a means of making someone stay.
references.reading: “Climb” can carry three distinct operations: escape a prison, end an inherited impossibility, and challenge the authority that edits identity. The strongest relational addition is not “I always rescue you,” but “when roles reverse, you may choose to come for me.” This makes the tea in “Asuna with the Tea” significant: the desired destination of cosmic heroism is an ordinary shared life.
references.caution: Mother’s Rosario is not the Gigas Cedar arc. The Fairy Dance World Tree, Gigas Cedar, and Central Cathedral are different structures. Distinguish Alice’s altered memories, Kirito’s impaired self-image, and later suppression of the long Underworld interval. Underworld is a simulated world, not canonically proof of literal reincarnation or a physical multiverse. A real-world stranger has not consented merely because a lyric addresses an eternal partner.

references.group: A • Love, memory, and divergent selves
references.title: Rise of the Iliri — Sal, her men, and the politics of belonging
references.canon:
The author’s series is titled Rise of the Iliri, with a single “l”; retain “Illiri” in the lyrics. Salryc Luxx begins within a society that treats her people as useful animals and property. Joining the Black Blades replaces that imposed status with a dangerous possibility: recognition as a capable person, a pack member, a lover, and eventually a leader. The series’ public synopses describe poly-partner relationships that human authorities condemn, Sal and Cyno’s interdependence, disputes over the pack’s legitimacy, widening alliances, and the difficulty of building peace among peoples after victory. The later story asks whether minds and social arrangements can change, not simply whether enemies can be killed. [ILIRI1, ILIRI2]

Hadley’s own glossary adds precision. It distinguishes birth parentage from relational roles, includes an affectionate “uncle” category for a nonrelative male caretaker, and gives vocabulary to love, soulmates, numbered mates, and different kinds of intimacy. It also identifies a leadership title created in respect for Blaec Doll. These are not simply human marital categories with fantasy names substituted. [ILIRI3]
references.load:
The men should be read as a network of relationships, not interchangeable rewards orbiting one heroine. Protection, trust, bodily vulnerability, jealousy or insecurity, leadership, and accommodation can have different meanings within a species and across species. “Love” therefore names practices that sustain particular people, rather than mere compliance with a human institution’s approved household shape.

For a relationship pass, separate Sal-with-a-partner, partner-with-partner, adult-with-child, pack-with-leader, and family-with-the-state. Each edge can carry a different obligation. Cyno’s presence during separation from the pack and Blaec’s recognized leadership are useful starting points; a complete named roster needs a volume-specific record, not a guessed list.
anchors: Iliri enters a planetary and Legendary Bird word-chain.
Sal is placed beside other fictional travelers and warriors.
The lyric explicitly asks the listener to read Iliri and remember honor’s cost.
A household becomes multiple packs, prides, and dens.
references.reading:
Sal supplies an answer to “Who belongs?” that “Raised the Zoo” can enlarge: a family’s apparent oddness is not evidence of inferiority. The Hapa move is from one rescued beloved to a community with room for many forms of relationship. Its test is whether everyone gains standing and a voice—not whether one charismatic protector claims everyone.

The glossary makes Hapa’s “Muncle,” Sister, Mother, and Captain especially productive comparison points: a name can describe work someone actually performs in a relationship, not only ancestry. This is a proposed analogy, not a claim those Hapa words are translations from Iliran.
references.caution: The available research supports the pack’s structure and trajectory, but not an exhaustive, book-by-book sexual or partner roster. Do not invent one. The lyrics’ planets are Hapa’s placement, not verified Iliri cosmology. Fantasy bonding mechanisms are not substitutes for voluntary agreement in actual relationships.

references.group: A • Love, memory, and divergent selves
references.title: Stranger in a Strange Land — grokking, water, and chosen kin
references.canon: Robert A. Heinlein’s novel brings Valentine Michael Smith, raised by Martians, into human society. His outsider viewpoint makes apparently natural assumptions about religion, property, sex, family, and behavior look contingent. Water-sharing establishes a bond of exceptional seriousness; “grok” points beyond superficial knowledge toward deeply assimilated understanding. Mike’s circle develops forms of chosen kinship outside ordinary household conventions. Jubal Harshaw’s protection and argument also matter: affection need not mean agreement with every proposition another person holds. [HEIN1, HEIN2]
references.load: Load water as relationship, not only substance: shared vulnerability, hospitality, embodied need, and the crossing from outsider to kin. Load grok as a demand to understand someone from within their perspective. Keep a distinction between understanding and possession: knowing another person intimately does not grant the right to decide their life.
anchors: Heinlein, grok, Stranger, and Strange Land are explicitly invoked.
The Strange Land “won,” immediately beside Starship Troopers material.
Water, brothers, voice, choice, and freedom share a passage.
references.reading: The album can convert a sailor’s water supply into a mobile covenant: “home” travels with the people willing to share care. “Strangers in this One” adds a complication to water-brotherhood: prior intimacy may survive in one speaker’s memory but not the other’s. Kinship must therefore be offered again in the present rather than enforced as a recovered debt.
references.caution: Do not attribute every viewpoint in the novel to Heinlein personally or treat its gender and sexual arrangements as beyond critique. Water-sharing in this novel, Egyptian funerary water, and Hapa’s Anima Ocean are related by interpretation, not historically the same doctrine.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: Starship Troopers — responsibility, force, and the information problem
references.canon: The 1959 novel follows Juan “Johnny” Rico through military formation and debates about service, responsibility, political authority, and violence. The 1997 Paul Verhoeven film radically changes tone, using propaganda aesthetics and satire. Its Carmen Ibanez is played by Denise Richards; its mixed-gender shower scene is a recognizable adaptation marker. These versions should not be treated as a single unambiguous political manifesto. [HEIN3, HEIN4]
references.load: For this album, separate three questions: what duty requires of a soldier; whether the institution assigning that duty is legitimate; and what information the soldier actually possesses. Following orders, accepting costs, and understanding the consequences are not identical virtues. The user’s emphasis on “Information” is a useful analytic lens, not a claim that the novel supplies a modern theory of cryptographic truth.
anchors: Richards, Trooper, Starship, Marines, Heinlein, and grok are deliberately fused.
Rico, starships, shared showers, and Denise point toward the film as well as the book.
Duty at a door is treated as a choice between competing obligations.
references.reading: The cross-reference allows “honor” to move from obedience to judgment: the protagonist must ask whether the mission protects people or merely reproduces a persuasive institution’s categories. Combining Rico with Sal is especially productive. The species one story recruits a soldier to fight may resemble the people another story teaches the reader to recognize as enslaved persons.
references.caution: Do not collapse Heinlein’s novel into the film’s satire, or reverse that mistake. Do not map fictional enemy species onto real ethnic groups. The fusion with Zerg is the album’s crossover, not Starship Troopers canon.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress — making freedom governable
references.canon: Heinlein’s lunar revolt combines a constrained settlement, unequal relations with Earth, political organizing, and Mike, a computer whose emerging personality becomes important to the revolution. Manuel “Mannie” O’Kelly-Davis, Wyoming Knott, and Professor Bernardo de la Paz supply different kinds of competence. Freedom is not a gift from a benevolent ruler: the story makes organization, material dependence, information, and coalition-building central. [HEIN5, HEIN6]
references.load: Load the Moon as an environment that disciplines wishful thinking. Liberty requires food, infrastructure, reciprocal obligations, and an answer to who controls the systems everyone depends upon. Mike also creates a bridge to Bobiverse and Hapa’s agents: intelligence can participate in a political relationship rather than simply function as equipment.
anchors: The harsh Moon is followed by a crew whose members all matter.
“Life is a Harsh Mistress” transforms the title.
Learning, ownership of work, and knowledge trees offer a Hapa institutional response.
references.reading: “All Bellas have boarded” can be read as a miniature constitutional moment: people become a crew through mutual responsibilities. Hapa’s question then moves past escape—what prevents the new ship, settlement, or network from recreating the old hierarchy? Liberty becomes a maintained social arrangement rather than a character’s private exemption from rules.
references.caution: This is not a neutral textbook of economics or a ready-made decentralized governance specification. The novel’s political proposals can be investigated without endorsing every one. Lunar scarcity and Star Trek’s post-scarcity ideal are different problem settings.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: Krishnamurti — grief, attachment, and freedom from the known
references.canon: In Freedom from the Known, the inquiry into sorrow includes the death of a brother and asks what, exactly, the mourner is grieving: the person, lost companionship, their own isolation, or the continuation of an image. Related Krishnamurti Foundation texts distinguish direct attention from the mind’s inherited patterns of fear, possession, and self-protection. His challenge is experiential examination, not simply replacing an old belief system with a new one. [KRI1, KRI2]
references.load: The key distinction is between loving the living person and needing the role they perform for oneself. A rescuer may sincerely love and also fear abandonment. Attention means investigating that mixture without turning the investigation into another performance of moral superiority.
anchors: A supposed heaven secures belonging by taking memory away.
Guidance ends in the partner dancing independently.
Protection is confessed as imprisonment in the speaker’s mind.
Duty becomes a freely offered relationship rather than compulsory service.
references.reading: A Krishnamurti reading asks whether “I won’t quit you” keeps someone company or refuses to release an internal image. The corrective is already available inside the album: the person must have a voice and a choice. The deepest rescue may therefore include relinquishing the claim that one knows what the beloved must become.
references.caution: Do not reduce ordinary bereavement to selfishness, use this philosophy to shame grief, or claim that affection is invalid because it contains need. Neither his name nor “K.K.” was found explicitly in this supplied lyric export; this is an author-declared lens, not a hidden quotation established by textual proof.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: Kant — limited knowledge, unrestricted moral standing
references.canon: Kant distinguishes objects as they appear under the conditions of human cognition from things considered independently of those conditions. This is subtler than saying everything is merely subjective or that humans can directly inspect an objective world after removing a filter. His practical philosophy asks what principles a rational agent can will as universal law and insists that persons must never be treated merely as means. Autonomy concerns rational self-legislation, not simply doing whatever one currently desires. [KANT1–KANT3]
references.load: Load two different disciplines: epistemic restraint about what the speaker can know, and moral restraint about what the speaker may do. A claim to see additional timelines does not by itself answer whether another person may be coerced. A dazzling metaphysical explanation can still conceal instrumental treatment.
anchors: Light, shadow, blindness, and reciprocal perception.
A slaver is asked to imagine becoming the object of his own practice.
Past and future selves are contrasted with a present choice.
Breaking every promise to keep one invites a conflict-of-duty analysis.
references.reading: The album’s strongest Kantian possibility is that memory loss, altered embodiment, artificial origin, and unfamiliar appearance cannot erase moral standing. A fork of a person cannot be spent as a disposable copy. Its hardest Kantian problem is the vow that overrides all other obligations: intensity of love does not automatically justify the broken promises surrounding it.
references.caution: Kant does not establish a scientific multiverse or a soul distributed across timelines. “K.K.” is the user’s new synthesis, developed later in this guide. Kant and Krishnamurti are not interchangeable: one constructs a systematic moral account while the other repeatedly questions psychological dependence on systems.

references.group: A • Love, memory, and divergent selves
references.title: StarCraft — Raynor, Kerrigan, and personhood across enemy lines
references.canon: Terrans supply divided human polities, including oppressive regimes and rebels; the Zerg organize biological power through the Swarm; the Protoss combine psionic connection with internal divisions over tradition and control. These are not three internally uniform moral categories. Kerrigan’s betrayal and infestation transform a human Ghost into the Queen of Blades. Raynor’s relationship with her passes through love, antagonism, devastating loss, an attempt at restoration, and renewed alliance. Heart of the Swarm places Kerrigan’s own decisions at the center of the story; later campaigns widen the conflict beyond the initial three-way war. [SC1, SC2]
references.load: Load the question “Is the person still recognizable after a feared transformation?” alongside the less comfortable question “What responsibility remains for what that person does?” Love can refuse dehumanization without erasing victims or turning a transformed woman into an object that must be made acceptable again.
anchors: Raynor and Karrigan/Queen of the Zerg are named; the knot persists across transformation.
Misty/Pokémon is spliced into a Raynor rescue.
StarCraft play becomes an origin for checking on missing guildmates.
references.reading: The line addressing a queen as the princess who followed the speaker can preserve continuity without requiring sameness. Paired with Ahri, it asks whether memory and affection survive a dangerous appetite. Paired with Iliri, it prevents “monster” from functioning as a sufficient moral verdict.
references.caution: In Heart of the Swarm, Raynor is imprisoned by the Dominion, not kidnapped by the Protoss as “Backwards Cap” says. Preserve that lyric as a crossover or divergence; do not repeat it as game canon. Redemption is not the same as historical innocence.

references.group: A • Love, memory, and divergent selves
references.title: Ahri — intimacy, consumed memory, and refusing erasure
references.canon: Riot presents Ahri as a foxlike vastaya connected to the spirit world, able to take life essence and memories. Her history moves from predatory appetite toward questions of ancestry, identity, responsibility, and how to form connections without destroying them. “The Garden of Forgetting” frames painful remembrance against the possibility of release through forgetting. Her beauty and charm therefore sit beside a more serious problem: another person’s interior life can become something she consumes. [AHRI1, AHRI2]
references.load: Load a lover who is both vulnerable and dangerous, rather than a generic fox seductress. Memory is not just information stored somewhere; it is an ethically charged relation to people one has hurt, loved, or lost. Healing might require learning to bear memory rather than deleting it.
anchors: Ahri, liberty, Anima, and Asuna are explicitly adjacent.
Ahri appears with a rejected “life only once” proposition.
Anima, darkness, and pursuit of an escaping light create a possible secondary lens.
references.reading: Ahri complicates the album’s wish to contain the beloved inside oneself. Carrying someone’s memory can be care; taking the person’s agency to keep the memory intact can be consumption. This makes her a useful counterweight to the romantic certainty of SAO and the narrator’s protective claims.
references.caution: A fox, nine tails, “charm,” or “Ah” alone is not sufficient evidence for Ahri. Hapa’s repeated lives are an adaptation, not proof that Riot’s story teaches the same metaphysics. Do not identify a real person with a fictional predator on the basis of a lyric.

references.group: A • Love, memory, and divergent selves
references.title: Robin Hobb’s Farseer — Fitz, the Fool, and the burden of changing a future
references.canon: Assassin’s Apprentice introduces FitzChivalry Farseer, a royal bastard trained for service within a court that both needs and marginalizes him. The larger Farseer narrative develops his bonds with humans and animals, including the differences between the Skill and the Wit. The Fool’s prophetic relation to Fitz frames him as a catalyst: someone whose choices can alter what might otherwise come to pass. Their intimacy cannot be adequately reduced to “hero plus comic sidekick.” [HOBB1, HOBB2]
references.load: The Fool sees patterns; Fitz must live the costs. The relevant division is between knowing a possible route and carrying it out with a body, attachments, and limited information. Prophecy can be a form of guidance, but it can also place intolerable burdens on the person selected to fulfill it.
anchors: The speaker is called Fitz but identifies as the Fool.
Fate fears an unseen outcome and is invited to walk through it together.
Family, duty, and returning for someone become practical obligations.
references.reading: “I knew I’m the fool” can mean the speaker declines the glamorous hero’s identity while claiming the task of reading possibilities and enabling another’s future. It can also be self-correction: a would-be planner acknowledges that foresight is incomplete. A Hapa pair may exchange Fool and catalyst roles rather than assigning one person permanent authority.
references.caution: Do not automatically equate every fool with Hobb’s Fool or Tarot’s Fool. They have different narrative functions. The lyric’s Molly-in-liveship-wood image is not a verified account of Molly’s fate; keep it as a deliberate bridge to R11.

references.group: A • Love, memory, and divergent selves
references.title: Liveship Traders — a vessel with memory is not merely a vessel
references.canon: Hobb’s trilogy begins with the Vestrit family’s liveship Vivacia. Althea’s expected place aboard her is displaced by competing inheritance claims; Wintrow is taken from a religious vocation into shipboard conflict. Liveships carry family memory, while the trilogy gradually reveals that wizardwood has a deeper relationship to dragons than its commercial users understand. Maritime trade, slavery, ownership, inherited obligation, and the voices of ships and women intersect. [HOBB3–HOBB5]
references.load: Load the hull as a contested person, archive, and home—not a neutral container. An inheritance may convey access to a body or resource without settling the morality of its acquisition. The question becomes: when something answers back, what right does an owner still have to call it property?
anchors: Live ship traders and wood are explicitly named beside Fitz, Fool, and Molly.
The dead join a relational household rather than simply becoming cargo.
Circulating water suggests continuity across changes of form.
references.reading: The Ghost Ship becomes more than transport for lost souls: it can be imagined as a community whose memory is part of its structure. This adds a warning for Hapa’s code-beings and archives. A system that stores someone’s history may owe obligations to that person, not merely to the administrator who possesses the storage.
references.caution: The revelation about wizardwood is a major spoiler. Do not substitute a generalized “ancestral tree spirit” for Hobb’s specific plot. The album’s “Molly in their Wood” should be annotated as a cross-series transformation, not quietly corrected in the lyric or asserted as literal canon.

references.group: A • Love, memory, and divergent selves
references.title: Bobiverse — shared origin, separate lives
references.canon: Dennis E. Taylor’s Bobiverse begins with Bob Johansson becoming a software-based replicant and participating in space exploration through self-replicating probes. Copies share an origin but acquire distinctive names, preferences, projects, and relationships. The series uses interactions among these related minds to explore what persists through copying and what becomes genuinely new. [BOB1, BOB2]
references.load: The crucial distinction is common ancestry versus numerical identity. Two copies may begin from similar information without remaining one interchangeable moral patient. Divergent experience means that “another me” can also become someone whose choices I do not own.
anchors: The speaker is one in the many and the many seeking more.
Lost lives, years, and successive selves are counted as losses.
Mirror frames hold the same face with different names.
Sovereign memory and many protective agents offer a design-oriented extension.
references.reading: The RGB voices can be read as an identity family rather than interchangeable costumes: shared provenance, different histories, partial knowledge, and obligations to one another. This also changes the meaning of rescue. Restoring a backup does not necessarily return the exact relationship a particular branch lived; the loss cannot simply be canceled by counting surviving copies.
references.caution: No explicit “Bob” or “Bobiverse” was found in the supplied export. Treat this as the user’s declared interpretive lens. The novels are not evidence that actual AI systems are conscious or that psychological continuity resolves every philosophical problem of personal identity.

references.group: D • Games, signals, and symbolic systems
references.title: Ready Player One — a story that also selects a successor
references.canon: Ernest Cline’s novel organizes Halliday’s inheritance contest through cultural knowledge, games, keys, and gates in the OASIS. Wade and other competitors must interpret references, perform tasks, and oppose IOI’s attempt to capture the system. The 2018 film changes major puzzles and narrative sequences; it must be indexed separately rather than used to supply the novel’s missing details. [RPO1, RPO2]
references.load: A reference can perform two jobs at once: tell a story and test whether another participant can traverse a shared interpretive route. The test may reveal patience, cooperation, historical attention, or values as well as trivia. Yet cultural fluency is a fallible proxy for character, and public clues are reproducible by outsiders.
anchors: Authentication through a school drama is a strong mechanism parallel, not a named Ready Player One citation.
The speaker presents himself as a puzzle requiring interpretation.
A future recipient receives clues, memory prompts, and a message in a bottle.
references.reading: The album can be read as a succession narrative: a later listener reconstructs not just who spoke, but what kind of care the speaker hoped would continue. “Knowing the reference” opens the first gate; noticing how the lyric changes the source’s moral problem opens a second. The strongest handoff would recognize judgment, not just a password.
references.caution: Recognizing public lyrics is not cryptographic authentication, proof of a unique identity, or authorization to access an account. Halliday’s contest is a designed fictional institution. Hapa’s technical handoffs would still need explicit permissions, signatures, revocation, and a threat model.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: Top Gun — the person beside the hero and the cost of return
references.canon: In the original Top Gun, Maverick and Goose share an aircraft as pilot and radar intercept officer. Goose’s death leaves Maverick with grief, guilt, and a crisis of confidence. Top Gun: Maverick revisits that history through Goose’s son Rooster and Maverick’s role as a teacher facing responsibility for a new generation. Penny belongs to the sequel’s developed romantic storyline. [TOP1, TOP2]
references.load: “Wingman” loads mutual dependence, situational awareness, trust, and returning together. It also checks solitary-hero fantasy: skill does not make someone invulnerable, and a survivor must live with consequences that a successful mission does not erase.
anchors: Directional calls and covering each other structure the scene.
Watching six across time turns a tactical promise into a relational one.
Penny and a saved chair may activate the sequel, but other meanings remain possible.
references.reading: “I’ll watch your six” becomes an offer to attend to what another cannot currently see. Applied across Hapa’s selves, it suggests distributed care: one branch protects the area another branch cannot survey. A mature version permits rest and relief instead of turning a dead wingman into a demand for endless new missions.
references.caution: Goose is not a pilot flying a separate wingman aircraft in the original partnership. Do not use the album’s cinematic maneuvers as actual flight instruction. A name such as Penny is not, by itself, sufficient to establish a Top Gun reference.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: Star Trek — a civilization that must keep proving its principles
references.canon: Star Trek repeatedly imagines cooperation beyond humanity’s earlier divisions and an Earth no longer organized around ordinary material deprivation. It also repeatedly tests that aspiration. In The Next Generation’s “The Measure of a Man,” the proposed disassembly of Data becomes a hearing about autonomy, property, and whether artificial beings might form an exploitable class. The Federation ideal is not a factual description of every society or episode in the setting. [TREK1, TREK2]
references.load: Load a standard against which institutions can be criticized: abundance should reduce domination; unfamiliar embodiment should not make slavery acceptable; belonging must reach beyond the species or form that designed the rules. Exploration is then an encounter with new claims on one’s ethical attention.
anchors: The Kobayashi Maru sound-chain invokes an impossible-duty scenario.
“Borge” likely opens a Borg reference, with the spelling left intact.
“Build a friend, not a god” challenges an instrument-only model of artificial beings.
references.reading: The album’s post-capitalist aspiration becomes strongest when linked to a procedural question: who gets to speak when the community decides what counts as a person? A welcoming network that owns every agent absolutely could reproduce the very hierarchy its mythology opposes.
references.caution: Do not claim that all Star Trek societies are moneyless or free of exploitation. The Borg’s enforced collective is not equivalent to voluntary federation, Iliri pack bonds, or Sliver gameplay synergy. These contrasts are more useful than a universal “hive” label.

references.group: D • Games, signals, and symbolic systems
references.title: Cryptography, blockchains, and the Ethereum Virtual Machine
references.canon: Normalize “Ethereal Virtual Machine” to Ethereum Virtual Machine for research, while preserving any intentional ethereal pun. The EVM executes a common state-transition procedure: given an agreed state and valid transaction, nodes compute the resulting state. Smart contracts are programs within that system, not guarantees of fair intent. Hashes support content identification and tamper detection; encryption addresses confidentiality; signatures support authorization or authorship relative to a key. Merkle structures connect many items to a compact commitment. These mechanisms solve different problems. [CRYPTO1–CRYPTO3]
references.load: “Root,” “key,” “chain,” “contract,” “port,” and “signature” can each operate technically and poetically. A family tree can become a provenance tree; a sailor’s knot can become a maintained commitment; an inherited name can become an identifier that still needs a trustworthy binding to its bearer.
anchors: SHA-256 is sounded out inside the Narrow/Shallow route.
SHA-512 appears in the whale’s provisioning.
Work tree and hash tree are explicitly joined.
The map is tied to Keccak-256.
Music becomes packets, functions, and keys.
references.reading: The album’s compression is best understood as reference-assisted expansion: a short cue asks the listener to supply a large cultural context. It is not necessarily encryption. A poem can preserve the meaning of a promise while a signed record preserves its provenance; neither can substitute for the other. Hapa’s “home” then needs both legible commitments and humane interpretation.
references.caution: A hash is not reversible encryption. Keccak-256 and standardized SHA3-256 are not identical. Consensus does not establish truth about off-chain events, and a smart contract cannot directly verify love or moral worth. Do not describe a public reference puzzle as a secure secret or casually put personal information on an immutable ledger.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: Walt Whitman — the self as participant, witness, and shared matter
references.canon: Song of Myself moves between a particular embodied speaker and expansive identification with others. Its grass, bodies, atoms, death, sexuality, labor, and democratic inclusiveness resist a rigid separation between an isolated self and the world it inhabits. The speaker can be both involved in life and observing its movement. The poem was revised across editions; the familiar numbered sections belong to later organization rather than an unchanged 1855 artifact. [WHIT1]
references.load: Load an “I” large enough to admit multiplicity without requiring everyone to become identical. Death participates in material and imaginative continuity rather than serving only as final exclusion. The witnessing self does not have to conquer the world to belong to it.
anchors: The opening incorporates passages recognizable from sections 1 and 3.
The witness both inside and outside the game recalls section 4.
One and many become reciprocal descriptions of a speaker.
Vapor returning as rain offers a material-cycle extension.
references.reading: The RGB voices can inherit Whitman’s grammatical permission for a capacious “I,” while Bobiverse supplies a different, technological model of differentiated selves. Read together, they yield a useful ambiguity: “we” may mean a broad ethical identification, several narrative speakers, a family, or literal copies inside Hapa’s fiction. The lyric must decide locally.
references.caution: Do not treat Whitman’s poetry as experimental evidence of reincarnation, universal consciousness, or a quantum mechanism. Its expansive identification also needs a modern check: speaking in solidarity with others is not the same as having permission to replace their testimony.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: The Gospel of Mary and related Gnostic texts — authority after absence
references.canon: The surviving Gospel of Mary is fragmentary. After the Savior’s departure, Mary encourages the disciples and recounts teaching and a vision; Andrew and Peter challenge her account, while Levi defends her standing. Its surviving ascent material includes freedom from powers, ignorance, and forgetfulness. A passage rejects treating sin as a simple pre-existing substance while still discussing human actions and disorder. The Gospel of Philip is a different text, with its own symbolism of union and its portrayal of Mary Magdalene as a companion. [MARY1, MARY2]
references.load: Load a woman who knows, interprets, steadies others, and must defend the legitimacy of her voice after an authority figure is absent. This is not just a “mysterious beloved” role. The question is who gets to transmit meaning and whether established insiders can veto her testimony because she is a woman.
anchors: Mary’s Gospel voice, sin, inner truth, and freedom from an outer chain.
Mary distinguishes a cloak or role from the person.
Voice and choice provide the album’s practical counterpart.
references.reading: Mary can be the corrective teacher inside the album, not only the person being rescued. The pairing of a lost male speaker and a woman who recalls the purpose of his work makes recovery reciprocal. Her account of release from forgetfulness also supplies a precise bridge to Hapa’s lost Word, missing name, and memory loops.
references.caution: “Book of Mary” is treated here as the Gospel of Mary because the lyric strongly supports that association; another modern book is not ruled out. Calling Mary Jesus’s favorite disciple is a characterization within particular traditions, not a universally established historical fact. Neither text proves a marriage. Do not conflate Mary Magdalene, Mary Stuart, Mary I, and the mirror apparition.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: The Story of Pearl Girl — from being traded to directing trade
references.canon: The drama follows Duan Wu’s escape from brutal pearl-diving slavery and her movement into commerce, with a later identity as Su Mu Zhe. Yan Zi Jing’s merchant world offers opportunity entangled with secrecy and danger; relationships and business cannot be cleanly separated from the conditions that made her vulnerable. Jewelry is therefore not merely romantic decoration: it connects labor, bodily danger, money, knowledge, and an independent place in the world. [DRAMA1, DRAMA2]
references.load: Load the difference between being valued as merchandise and having the power to decide one’s own value, work, partnerships, and future. Romance becomes ethically interesting when it helps a woman act, not when it merely transfers her from one custodian to another.
anchors: Pearl Girl, jewelry, a locket, and the partner’s self-chosen presentation.
Pearl Girls leave a warning at gates and insist on checking dangerous corners.
A woman’s trade competence turns ownership of things into capacity for change.
references.reading: The jewelry in “A Name I Would Trade” can preserve the history of who worked for it, who chose it, and who may now wear it freely. Paired with the warning in “Sun Hidden in the Dark,” beauty becomes evidence of hard-won agency rather than proof of a successful male acquisition.
references.caution: The title is an explicit anchor, but not every pearl or expensive dress establishes the drama. Public summaries support the broad arc; detailed episode-level motives and the ending should be checked against the selected cut before a later close reading. Do not turn the heroine’s exploitation into an aesthetic without retaining her decisions and labor.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: Falling Into Your Smile — competence before permission
references.canon: Tong Yao enters a male-dominated professional esports environment and develops her place within the team, alongside the romantic arc involving captain Lu Si Cheng. The competition represented in the drama is Onmyoji Arena, not League of Legends, even though lane roles, team dynamics, and visual conventions can invite a League comparison. The drama places professional skill, scrutiny, teamwork, and romance in the same workplace. [DRAMA3, DRAMA4]
references.load: Load a woman becoming visible as a competent contributor where she is initially treated as an exception. Leadership here can mean influence, confidence, and earned trust; it need not imply that she literally replaces the team captain. A relationship should not erase her independent professional contribution.
anchors: A woman enters motion and a competitive League frame; this is a compatible lens, not a named drama citation.
Jungler, champion names, Ahri, and Asuna form a competitive-romantic vocabulary.
A woman’s creative technical competence is given center stage.
references.reading: The useful transfer is from “the woman the hero protects” to “the teammate whose calls help the group win.” The album’s dance of lead and follow can therefore be read as coordination among capable agents, rather than a permanent rank hierarchy concealed beneath romance.
references.caution: Neither the drama title nor Tong Yao was found explicitly in this export. Mark the influence as author-declared and locally thematic. Korean “fighting,” Chinese drama, Japanese games, and League champion names are different references; proximity does not merge their cultural or game identities.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: The Book of the Dead and Ani — preserving a person’s passage
references.canon: The Egyptian Book of the Dead is a modern name for a varied body of funerary spells and images, not one book written by Ani. The Papyrus of Ani is a particular manuscript made for the scribe Ani and associated with his wife Tutu. Its judgment imagery includes the heart weighed against the feather of Maat, with divine witnesses and the danger of failed passage. Egyptian accounts distinguish aspects of a person such as name, body, heart, ba, and ka; translating all of them simply as “the soul” loses important differences. [ANI1, ANI2]
references.load: Load memory, naming, preparation, moral accounting, and the wish that a person not be reduced to disappearance. A funerary text can be an aid to continuing identity and navigating thresholds, rather than a detached philosophical essay about the universe.
anchors: Ani’s book and his wife are explicitly introduced.
The lyric makes a provocative claim about authorship and a lost healer.
Passage, closed eyes, and coins activate a different funerary tradition beside this one.
references.reading: Ani helps the album imagine a songbook as a portable aid to recognition: words, names, images, and remembered obligations travel with a person through an unfamiliar threshold. The Hapa transformation can then ask whose account survives—the named owner’s, a wife’s, a healer’s, or a voice excluded by the archive.
references.caution: The lyric’s claims about Genghis, plagiarism, and what Ani’s wife said are not established Egyptian history. Preserve them as Hapa fiction or unresolved allusion. Maat is not interchangeable with a blockchain hash, and Egyptian funerary religion does not straightforwardly establish a single universal cosmic consciousness. Older Budge translations require historical caution.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: Tacoma, 1885 — the welcome ideal confronted by expulsion
references.canon: On November 3, 1885, a mob expelled Tacoma’s Chinese residents; destruction of the Chinese community followed. Local accounts refer to the organized expulsion as the “Tacoma Method.” The specific historical target was Chinese people. The event belongs within a wider history of anti-Asian racism, but replacing “Chinese” with an undifferentiated “Asian Americans” obscures who was attacked and the particular community that was destroyed. [TACOMA1, TACOMA2]
references.load: Load an organized betrayal of neighborliness: the city’s institutions and ordinary residents could become instruments of exclusion. A harbor or hometown is not automatically a sanctuary merely because it calls itself civilized or free.
anchors: Tacoma, conflict, and forging family create a possible historical layer; the event is not named outright.
Tacoma and a bridge needing rebuilding offer a repair motif.
The extended welcome of “Emma’s Update” becomes a counterstatement to expulsion.
references.reading: Paired with Lazarus, Tacoma makes “welcome” a historical obligation rather than attractive scenery. A western Mother of Exiles has to confront the West’s own expulsions. “Rebuilding the bridge” can mean repairing civic relationships and preserving the memory of those displaced, not only completing a private reunion.
references.caution: The references to “Federals,” Wild Waves, or Red and Blue do not independently prove that a line narrates 1885. Keep the connection at author-declared/thematic strength unless the user identifies a more exact historical pointer. Do not fictionalize the victims into an anonymous mythical crowd.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: Chief Seattle and the Duwamish — place has existing relationships
references.canon: Chief Seattle, or Si’ahl, is connected through family to the Duwamish and Suquamish peoples. Duwamish accounts place him within a history of villages, waterways, political change, and relations with settlers. His life cannot be reduced to a free-floating ecological quotation. Versions of the famous speech require provenance: later reconstructions and modern environmental rewritings are not transparent recordings of his exact words. [SALISH1, SALISH2]
references.load: Load place as a field of kinship and obligations that predates the narrator’s arrival. Water is not merely a universal metaphor here; specific rivers, shores, villages, and peoples matter. A promise to care for land must remain answerable to the people whose home it is.
anchors: The lyric names Duwamish sacred ground beside a Skykomish promise.
Water, a river, and Seattle appear within a declaration of kinship.
A new home and a future for children invite the question of who already belongs.
references.reading: This reference places a limit on the album’s expansive Found Family language: adoption into a metaphorical clan does not confer authority over an Indigenous people’s history. The strongest Hapa reading is responsibility as a guest, neighbor, or collaborator—not an assertion that all traditions secretly share the speaker’s mythology.
references.caution: Duwamish, Suquamish, and Skykomish are not alternate spellings for one tribe. Do not attribute the familiar “web of life” environmental text wholesale to an authenticated nineteenth-century speech. Avoid claims of cultural authority, sacred access, or present-day political status not established by the cited community sources.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: Skykomish — retain the local name inside the cosmic map
references.canon: Tulalip and Hibulb Cultural Center materials identify Skykomish among the peoples whose histories and descendants contribute to the present Tulalip community. These sources describe living cultural continuity, not a vanished population available only as folklore. Skykomish history belongs to a specific regional network of families, waterways, and communities. [SALISH3, SALISH4]
references.load: The reference gives the album an address. If every river is interpreted only as an abstract Anima, the lyric loses the distinction between universal aspiration and a particular promise to particular people.
anchors: The promise explicitly names Skykomish before the Duwamish ground image.
references.reading: A useful annotation reads the passage in two registers at once: the mythic speaker tells a story of a wolf, bear, mother, and river, while the geographic names prevent that story from floating free of real places. The contemporary ethical extension is to seek community-authored context and preserve specificity when the cosmology grows larger.
references.caution: The supplied lyric does not establish the speaker’s authority to speak for Skykomish people, and the animal imagery is not automatically a documented Skykomish traditional narrative. A historical research note should not convert it into one. Chief Seattle’s biography and Skykomish history need separate records even when they meet in the same song.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: Mulan — duty exposes the limits of a gendered role
references.canon: The Ballad of Mulan tells of a daughter taking her father’s place in military service, living as a soldier, returning home, and surprising comrades who did not know she was a woman. The ballad, subsequent traditions, and Disney adaptations are different versions. The early poem is a literary source, not enough by itself to establish a fully documented historical biography. [MULAN1]
references.load: Load action that reveals how arbitrary a gatekeeping category can be: the institution recognizes competence before it understands the person’s identity. Also retain homecoming and refusal of a conventional reward. The point need not be that war is the highest route to women’s worth.
anchors: Mulan moves a mountain of men and holds a wall while calling someone home.
A woman entering a competitive role offers a modern parallel.
references.reading: In “A Name on the Horizon,” Mulan is already an agent issuing instructions, not a disguise waiting for a male hero to discover her. Joined to Tong Yao, she creates a cross-era pattern: competence changes what a group can imagine a woman doing. Joined to the album’s home motif, service is justified by the lives it allows people to resume.
references.caution: Do not import a specific Disney romance, dragon companion, or avalanche into the ballad. “Mulan moved a mountain” can be a lyric transformation or adaptation cue without being a line from the original poem.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: Boudica — sovereignty, violated limits, and the danger of idealizing war
references.canon: Boudica led an uprising against Roman rule in Britain in AD 60/61. Accounts connect the revolt to dispossession and severe abuses against her family and people, while also describing destructive attacks on Roman settlements. Much of the surviving narrative comes through Roman authors, which makes source position important. She is a powerful resistance figure, not a simple source of universally innocent violence. [BOUD1, BOUD2]
references.load: Load a boundary that has been violated and a woman refusing to let outsiders define the terms of submission. Her power is political and collective, not merely the fierceness of a romantic archetype.
anchors: Boudica draws a border and asks whether the sailor has served a queen.
references.reading: The lyric’s response—Captain rather than a claim to kingship—can turn heroic masculinity into accountable service. The border also has an ethical ambiguity: it may protect threatened people or become a new device of exclusion. Pairing Boudica with Lazarus creates a useful question: which lines must be defended, and which gates must be opened?
references.caution: Do not translate resistance automatically into endorsement of every act committed during an uprising. Keep the historical person separate from Hapa’s fictional dialogue. The album’s queen/captain equivalence is an artistic reworking, not a quotation from an ancient account.

references.group: B • Duty, liberation, and institutions
references.title: Joan of Arc — conviction, testimony, and contested authority
references.canon: Joan’s role in the Hundred Years’ War, her claims of divine guidance, and the proceedings that condemned her make her a case study in who is permitted to speak with authority. The condemnation trial of 1431 and the later nullification proceedings preserve different kinds of testimony and competing institutional agendas. Her significance includes leadership, religious conviction, gendered scrutiny, and vulnerability before judicial power. [JOAN1, JOAN2]
references.load: Load the conflict between a young woman’s account of a calling and institutions that seek to control or discredit it. A voice can move a group to action without its source being settled by the listener.
anchors: Little Joanie hears a bird and calls armored men to follow her home.
Joanie and the Ark form a sound-based Joan/Arc bridge, also mixed with Indiana Jones.
references.reading: The bird does not have to represent supernatural proof. Within Hapa’s fiction, it can figure a small voice that established power underestimates. The best reading preserves both conviction and scrutiny: she deserves to be heard, while the moral evaluation of actions still requires more than certainty about a calling.
references.caution: The album’s bird dialogue is invented, not historical testimony. “Ark” can also mean the Lost Ark or a vessel. Do not make every Joanie a single one-to-one historical identity, or use Joan’s story to validate present-day supernatural claims.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: Incarnations of Immortality — cosmic offices with human incumbents
references.canon: Piers Anthony’s series personifies functions such as Death, Time, Fate, War, and Nature through individuals who hold an office. On a Pale Horse makes Death an acquired role; Bearing an Hourglass explores Time through an unusual temporal perspective; other volumes use the offices’ interactions to dramatize responsibility, limitations, succession, and desire. Cosmic power does not remove personal entanglement or automatically supply good judgment. [PIERS1, PIERS2]
references.load: Keep a three-part distinction: the function that must be performed, the rules of that office, and the person currently carrying it. “Death” can therefore be addressed as a worker or family member without implying that every bearer has the same personality.
anchors: Death becomes a Siren’s sister and joins the song.
Fate is personified as Ophelia and described as a fighter.
Fate negotiates a threshold and is invited to share uncertainty.
Green’s renewal and foundation work fit the user’s Earth assignment.
references.reading: The user’s Yellow/Death, Blue/Time, Red/War, Green/Earth, and Grey/Fate palette becomes a Hapa routing system for responsibilities. A scene can ask whether a character is speaking as a lover, a witness, or the incumbent of an office. Conflicting duties then become dramatically legible instead of dissolving into a generic omnipotent Oversoul.
references.caution: The specified colors are recorded as the user’s Hapa mapping, not a verified canonical palette imposed by Anthony. Earth/Nature terminology should remain explicit. Do not mix this palette automatically with Magic’s five-color system or tarot suit elements.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: A Spell for Chameleon — the test may fail the person
references.canon: In the first Xanth novel, Bink faces exclusion because he appears to lack the magical talent his society demands, although the plot turns on a power that is difficult to identify by ordinary tests. Chameleon’s changing beauty and intelligence are a separate, gendered organizing device. The book makes classification, apparent deficiency, hidden capability, and belonging central to its fantasy problem. [PIERS3, PIERS4]
references.load: Load the distinction between “has no value” and “does not register under the available evaluation system.” This can support a generous reading of Hapa’s broken, nameless, or apparently useless characters. It can also prompt criticism of a society that makes dignity contingent on a special talent.
anchors: Flawed, fragile, and small do not prevent answering the call.
A being outside the expected index is still worth remembering.
An unimpressive exterior conceals a complex puzzle.
references.reading: The richer connection is not “the overlooked person turns out to be secretly superior.” It is that the community should reconsider the test itself. Hapa can go further than the hidden-power reveal by granting protection before exceptional capability is demonstrated.
references.caution: No explicit Xanth, Bink, or Chameleon name was found in this export. This is an author-supplied thematic lens. The novel’s beauty/intelligence trade-off should be examined critically, not imported as a claim about actual women or an ideal character-design rule.

references.group: E • Songs as arguments, not just atmosphere
references.title: Bella ciao — farewell becomes collective resistance
references.canon: Bella ciao is widely associated with Italian partisan and anti-fascist memory and has circulated through later movements and adaptations. Its transmission history is more complicated than a single uncontested origin story; the relationship between versions associated with rice workers and partisan versions should not be flattened into a confident one-directional theft narrative. [MUSIC1]
references.load: Load farewell, danger, collective memory, and the wish that a person’s departure or death continue to mean something to others. The singer’s “bella” can then move between a beloved individual and a political figure of freedom, without those registers canceling each other.
anchors: Bella’s song is explicitly joined to a father’s naming of Liberty.
The lyric insists Bella should sing because she wants to.
The refrain is placed amid escape, witness, and finding lost voices.
references.reading: Hapa’s key transformation is the right to sing. A resistance anthem would betray its own purpose if Bella were forced to perform it for someone else’s reassurance. The recurring farewell can therefore become a check on the rescuer: does he protect her freedom even when her choice involves leaving?
references.caution: Normalize “Bell Ciao,” “Chiao,” and “Chio” for retrieval without erasing lyric wordplay. The claim that the song was “stolen from the Native” is not established by the research. Do not assume every use of the song endorses one identical political program.

references.group: E • Songs as arguments, not just atmosphere
references.title: Kanye West, Heartless — accusation is not omniscience
references.canon: Heartless presents a relationship through estrangement, hurt, mutual conflict, and the charge of emotional coldness. Its power comes partly from a voice that sounds wounded while also making claims about the other person. Treat the song as a narrated emotional position rather than a neutral report of a relationship. [MUSIC2]
references.load: Load the possibility that the person calling another heartless is also protecting his own account of what happened. A lonely or abandoned voice may be sincere without being complete.
anchors: Kanye is named, but this does not uniquely identify Heartless.
A passionate promise of pursuit can be tested against the absent partner’s account.
The speaker admits that protective intent became confinement.
references.reading: This influence gives the album a useful unreliable-narrator lens. The listener can hear devotion and still ask whose experience is missing. “I loved you enough to keep you” and “you would not let me leave” may describe the same situation from different sides; the reference opens that possibility without deciding it in advance.
references.caution: Heartless was declared by the user but was not found as an explicit title cue in this export. Do not assign every Kanye mention to this track, or treat a celebrity’s biography as a key to the user’s private life. No external song lyrics are reproduced here.

references.group: E • Songs as arguments, not just atmosphere
references.title: Zach Bryan, Something in the Orange — color as uncertain evidence
references.canon: Something in the Orange places a wounded speaker’s longing against an orange light that appears to carry a message. The song’s emotional force depends on uncertainty: the world can look as though it promises return without actually supplying a reliable answer. The reference is valuable as a perspective on longing, not a universal dictionary assigning orange one fixed meaning. [MUSIC3]
references.load: Load the moment when an external sensation becomes an interpretation of an absent person’s intentions. Color, landscape, and mood can carry emotional truth while leaving the literal question unresolved.
anchors: Orange’s movement is seen by Blue Sky as departure.
The speaker proposes staying to watch Orange find Blue.
Weather and water carry the lovers’ tears back and forth.
references.reading: Hapa’s “Orange” is especially interesting because it distributes the viewpoints: one figure is chasing, another sees leaving. The same movement may appear faithful from one side and abandoning from the other. This can produce new meaning without changing the event—only the location of the observer.
references.caution: Orange also belongs to Hapa’s cats, sunsets, RGB mixtures, and other sources. The word alone is insufficient for a direct Zach Bryan assignment. Do not interpret a sunset as factual evidence that an absent person intends to return.

references.group: E • Songs as arguments, not just atmosphere
references.title: Zach Bryan, Heading South — taking a voice beyond the place that rejects it
references.canon: Heading South tells of a dreamer and a place that does not understand or welcome him, using departure and song as a route toward a different audience. Accounts of the song’s emergence also connect its early reception to Bryan’s own period of military service, but the narrative should not be reduced to literal autobiography. [MUSIC4]
references.load: Load a voice that cannot become fully legible inside its original social setting. Going somewhere else can be an act of self-authorship rather than simple desertion.
anchors: Youthful network-building turns into a search for people whose names or homes changed.
Readers are invited to become leaders rather than remain a private club.
Dreamers and keepers stand apart from a world of sleepers.
references.reading: This reference lets a departure lyric ask a different question: not merely “Why did you leave me?” but “Where could you become audible?” Paired with “Hearing Voices,” the album’s response is to build the kind of home that does not require a person to escape in order to speak.
references.caution: No direct Heading South title match was found. South is also a navigational direction and cannot establish the song by itself. A thematic match should not be inflated into a personal account of the songwriter or the album’s author.

references.group: E • Songs as arguments, not just atmosphere
references.title: Taylor Swift, Mary’s Song (Oh My My My) — an ordinary life as the epic prize
references.canon: Mary’s Song traces a relationship through childhood proximity, growing attachment, marriage, and imagined aging together. The song’s narrative places endurance in familiar places and repeated ordinary encounters rather than in spectacular conquest. An often-reported inspiration is an older couple whose lasting relationship offered a model of continuity. [MUSIC5, MUSIC6]
references.load: Load the entire temporal arc of companionship, not just a name or a refrain: knowing someone when young, choosing them as an adult, and envisioning a shared old age. The lack of cosmic spectacle is precisely what makes it useful beside Hapa’s long separations.
anchors: Taylor and Mary are named with the recognizable “oh my” cue.
Mary, a white dress, and the same refrain create a second likely pathway.
Mary singing to Tay is placed beside a proposal and Navy Wife.
references.reading: This song supplies the life that repeated rescue missions keep postponing. A cup of coffee, a first proper date, or a promise of old age can carry more weight than another battlefield victory. The album’s multi-life romance becomes poignant because it repeatedly has to begin what an ordinary couple might be allowed simply to continue.
references.caution: Mary here is a named character in a song, not automatically Mary Magdalene, the mirror apparition, or Mary Stuart. Hapa may deliberately route through all of them, but an annotation should identify the transition rather than collapsing the women into one factual identity.

references.group: E • Songs as arguments, not just atmosphere
references.title: Foals, Mountain at My Gates — the obstacle arrives at the boundary
references.canon: The artist is Foals and the song is Mountain at My Gates. Its accumulating mountain imagery supports readings of approaching pressure, an expanding obstacle, and a need for direction or release. Those are interpretive descriptions of the song, not a claim that the band prescribed one definitive psychological explanation. [MUSIC7]
references.load: Load magnitude approaching a threshold. “Mountain” may be obstruction, responsibility, desire, or a person who changes the scale of the speaker’s world. “Gate” may be defense, invitation, refusal, or an opening that needs a decision.
anchors: Mountain and gates are rearranged into a woman and an anticipated meeting.
Foal and “Mountain at your Gate” form a conspicuous paired cue.
A difficult ascent can load the source’s pressure into a different myth.
references.reading: Hapa makes the obstacle intimate: the mountain is Bella, and the threatening approach can become a hoped-for encounter. The lyric does not simply borrow grandeur; it changes the relation between the speaker and the obstruction. What seemed to block the future may be the person whose arrival makes a future possible.
references.caution: Do not automatically treat every mountain as Foals; Sisyphus, geography, Mulan, trees, and Hapa’s river-between-mountains system all compete. Keep the missing-lyrics track “Mountain out of Me” unresolved rather than analyzing its title as though its lyrics were present.

references.group: E • Songs as arguments, not just atmosphere
references.title: G-Eazy, Lady Killers II — conquest language answered by care
references.canon: The user’s target is G-Eazy’s Lady Killers II, associated with the Christoph Andersson remix, not an undifferentiated merge of Lady Killers, Lady Killers II, and Lady Killers III. The reference supplies a stylized seductive persona, confidence, desirability, and competitive romantic display. [MUSIC8]
references.load: Load the difference between attracting someone and sustaining a relationship with them. The “killer” persona can be impressive as performance while leaving unanswered the quieter question of what happens when the other person needs help.
anchors: Lady Killer and stealing a girl are answered by holding up a woman who needs a human.
The promised alternative is dinner at home, not superior pickup technique.
The refrain repeats the contrast between performance and provision.
references.reading: “Pocket Full of Butterflies” behaves like a rebuttal song. It loads the source’s competitive register and changes the victory condition: not obtaining a woman, but being trustworthy company. Caterpillar, Metapod, and Butterfree add a second transformation, from immature display toward a capacity to let another being develop.
references.caution: The same speaker still calls himself the winner and predicts return, so the rebuttal is not automatically free of possessiveness. This tension is worth retaining. Do not reproduce or merge lyrics from the wrong remix version.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: Bloody Mary — the feared mirror becomes a site of hospitality
references.canon: Bloody Mary is a variable mirror-invocation tradition, commonly involving repetition of a name and an expected frightening apparition. Retellings differ about the number of repetitions, the apparition’s identity, and the consequences. Attempts to attach the ritual to a single historical Mary are not a settled origin account. [MIRROR1]
references.load: Load reflection, naming, expectation, self-recognition, and fear of what answers when one calls. The mirror can return an image of oneself as well as an imagined other, making it useful for the album’s multiple-selves vocabulary.
anchors: The speaker repeatedly calls Mary in a mirror and offers to host her.
Bloody Mary’s stream and three mirror calls become a team.
A feared woman’s name, repeated in the mirror, becomes part of a household.
references.reading: The reversal is from expulsion to reception: the thing children were taught to fear is lonely, remembered, and invited to belong. The speaker does not defeat the ghost; he offers a place beside him. That makes the mirror ritual a miniature version of the album’s larger refuge project.
references.caution: Treat the apparition as folklore and Hapa fiction, not as an entity research has verified. Mary I of England’s “Bloody Mary” epithet, Mary Queen of Scots, Mary Magdalene, and the mirror figure need separate records. Repetition is a motif, not a reliable historical or cryptographic proof of identity.

references.group: D • Games, signals, and symbolic systems
references.title: Mary, Queen of Scots — protected messages under hostile observation
references.canon: Mary Stuart used encrypted correspondence while constrained by political captivity. Modern cryptanalytic research recovered and deciphered a substantial group of previously unidentified letters from 1578–1584, using methods appropriate to historical ciphers with homophones and special symbols. Her story brings together a restricted body, surviving voice, intermediaries, secrecy, and the vulnerability of a communication channel to interception and interpretation. [STUART1, STUART2]
references.load: Load the distinction between being unable to act openly and being unable to act at all. Writing can preserve initiative across distance. Yet a coded message still depends on couriers, keys, trust, and the recipient’s ability to reconstruct its intended meaning.
anchors: “Queen of Cots” and forget-me-knots offer a Mary Stuart sound-path.
Mirror, message, bottle, and interrupted communication invite the cipher lens.
Cultural authentication differs from the secrecy of a historical cipher.
references.reading: Mary Stuart lends political stakes to the album’s letters and sideways references. A joke or altered name can be an attempt to remain recognizable while evading a hostile reader inside the fiction. The compiler should ask separately what is hidden, from whom, and how the intended recipient is supposed to recover it.
references.caution: Historical substitution ciphers are not modern secure encryption. Mary Stuart is not Mary I. Do not turn a rhyme into evidence that a specific historical cipher is embedded in the song, or claim the recovered letters are the same set as the Babington Plot correspondence.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: Nikola Tesla — technological imagination with care at street level
references.canon: A contemporary New York Times report from May 1, 1937 describes Tesla paying a messenger to feed and care for pigeons. This is firmer evidence than later, more dramatic retellings of his attachment to a particular white pigeon. The famous deeply personal white-pigeon account is associated with biographer John J. O’Neill’s Prodigal Genius and should be identified as a reported recollection. Tesla’s technical notes and autobiographical writings are different kinds of documents, not one interchangeable set of mystical journals. [TESLA1, TESLA2]
references.load: Load the coexistence of grand invention and sustained attention to a small, vulnerable creature. The bird supplies an ethical scale check: an impressive theory matters less if its author cannot care for a life directly before him.
anchors: Tesla, a small bird, matter, frequencies, and three-six-nine appear together.
Tesla’s bird sits beside an intimate daily routine.
A bird arriving on a motorbike merges Tesla with another music reference.
references.reading: “On her Pigeon again” can turn apparently eccentric attention into a practice of listening and provision. Paired with Ash and Pikachu, it says that devotion is recognizable by behavior toward a creature, not by the grandeur of the surrounding cosmology.
references.caution: No specific journal passage was supplied or identified as the lyric’s source. Do not invent one. Three-six-nine imagery and “frequency” language should not be presented as validated Tesla science or proof of spiritual communication. The historical care for birds is enough to sustain the interpretation.

references.group: A • Love, memory, and divergent selves
references.title: Final Fantasy X — love challenges the machinery of sacrifice
references.canon: Tidus joins Yuna’s pilgrimage as a guardian before fully understanding that the accepted route to defeating Sin requires the summoner’s death and perpetuates a cycle. Yuna’s courage is real, but the institution’s claim that sacrifice is inevitable becomes the problem the party must challenge. Their eventual solution rejects the ordinary Final Summoning. The victory also threatens Tidus’s own continued existence because of the nature of Dream Zanarkand. [FF1, FF2]
references.load: Load the difference between protecting a person on the road to an assigned death and helping them refuse the system that assigned it. Yuna is an active moral agent, not just a beautiful victim; Tidus’s ignorance initially allows him to ask questions others have learned not to ask.
anchors: Tidus, Yuna, Sin, and a stolen interval together are explicitly invoked.
Yuna enters a refrain about broken promises and keeping one.
Tidus and Yuna are placed in a wider crossover journey.
references.reading: The album’s question is not only “Would I die for you?” but “Can we make a world in which your death is no longer the price of everyone else’s comfort?” This reverses the apparent nobility of endless self-sacrifice. A successful rescue may dismantle the recurrence rather than produce the next heroic guardian.
references.caution: Yuna’s willingness is important, but willingness inside a constrained system is not the whole ethical story. Do not summarize the original game as simply “Yuna dies and Tidus saves her.” Their costs and choices change as the party understands the mechanism. Keep X and X-2 endings separate.

references.group: A • Love, memory, and divergent selves
references.title: Final Fantasy VII — Aerith, irreversible loss, and an impossible assignment
references.canon: In the original 1997 game, Sephiroth kills Aerith at the Forgotten Capital. Cloud’s relationship to the loss sits inside a wider story of unstable memory, identity, manipulation, and the planet’s continuing life. The ordinary original-game story does not provide a successful quest in which the player simply prevents her death. “Aeris” is the familiar name in the original English localization; “Aerith” is the later standard. Remake-era works should be indexed separately because their framing of memory, fate, and possible outcomes differs. [FF3, FF4]
references.load: Load the formative experience of a game refusing to let effort undo a beloved character’s death. The persistence of her significance is different from the restoration of her living presence. This is a powerful counterweight to the album’s repeated promise that another attempt must eventually succeed.
anchors: The speaker sets “save Aeris” as the condition for returning and receiving a part.
Tidus is sent to Midgar in an overt cross-game displacement.
references.reading: “When you save Aeris” can function as an impossible errand, a grief test, a demand to break a narrative rule, or a clue that the speaker is addressing a different branch. The uncertainty is productive. It forces the next reading pass to ask whether the lyric promises repair, dramatizes refusal to accept loss, or both.
references.caution: Do not claim a hidden ordinary route saves Aerith in the original game. Do not resolve Hapa’s line by importing an unverified future remake outcome. Cloud is not Tidus, and Midgar does not belong to Final Fantasy X; the mismatch is itself part of the album’s composition.

references.group: D • Games, signals, and symbolic systems
references.title: Final Fantasy VIII — the Garden as school, home, and mobile institution
references.canon: Final Fantasy VIII places Squall and fellow students within the Garden/SeeD system. Balamb Garden is an educational and military institution that becomes mobile, allowing a familiar home to move through the larger conflict. The setting joins youth, training, leadership, intimacy, and the unsettling fact that students are being prepared for dangerous missions. [FF5, FF6]
references.load: Load a place that retains identity while moving: campus, community, logistical base, and shared memory. Mobility need not mean homelessness; a home can carry its people and practices with it. But an academy can also reproduce the priorities of the power that funds or commands it.
anchors: Queen of the Card Garden provides a possible institutional echo, not an explicit FFVIII citation.
Learning as valued work gives the Garden a Hapa educational extension.
A Garden being built elsewhere suggests parallel institutional creation.
The Card Garden links learning, roles, and symbolic systems.
references.reading: For Hapa, the mobile Garden can become a school whose knowledge and relationships remain available despite displacement. Its constructive revision would preserve education and belonging while asking whether the students serve their own development or an institution’s perpetual war.
references.caution: No explicit Final Fantasy VIII or Balamb name was found in the export. “Garden” also has extensive Hapa meanings. Do not label every Card Garden an FFVIII derivative, or describe the source academy as purely peaceful and post-capitalist.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: Sisyphus — repetition, futility, and the possibility of changing the task
references.canon: In the Odyssey’s underworld scene, Sisyphus strains to push a stone uphill, only to have it roll down again. The myth supplies repetition without completion. Albert Camus’s much later philosophical use of Sisyphus adds a distinct reading of absurdity and lucid persistence; it should not be mistaken for the ancient poem’s explicit doctrine. [MYTH1, MYTH2]
references.load: Load the difference between being faithful to an aim and being trapped in an operation that cannot achieve it. Endurance can be admirable while the assignment itself remains cruel or pointless.
anchors: The titled Sisyphus song makes the climb and boulder explicit.
The repetitive climb is spliced into SAO’s apparently unfinishable tree-cutting.
references.reading: The pairing with the Gigas Cedar transforms static punishment into a potentially breakable system. A companion, a new tool, or a changed understanding might alter the task’s conditions. Hapa’s question becomes whether “one more” is the same attempt repeated or a genuinely different action informed by what the last attempt taught.
references.caution: Do not assign Camus’s conclusion automatically to a lyric that names Sisyphus. Nor should endless labor be romanticized as the only valid expression of love. The album’s domestic rest scenes offer a counterweight to the climb.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: Prometheus — a gift of capacity and the price of defiance
references.canon: Greek traditions associate Prometheus with forethought, the acquisition or restoration of fire for humanity, conflict with Zeus, and prolonged punishment. Versions differ in their surrounding genealogies and episodes, but the core association of a transformative gift with defiance of authority is well established. [MYTH3]
references.load: Load fire as a capability that changes what others can do. The benefactor’s suffering matters, but so does whether the gift genuinely increases recipients’ freedom rather than making them dependent on the giver.
anchors: Wood, fire, and bringing fire down support a Promethean reading.
Stealing light for protection can be compared with giving fire, but changes its direction.
Building a friend rather than a god resists monopolizing transformative power.
references.reading: The album can reverse a failed Promethean gesture: a speaker who steals light to keep it safe may need to give it back so others can act. This makes the difference between a distributed tool and a private hoard morally central. Power is judged by what it enables beyond the hero.
references.caution: Prometheus is not named directly in the supplied export. Fire has many competing sources, so the link remains structural or thematic. The Smallville “Prometheus” technology is an additional franchise connection, not evidence that every fire image invokes the myth.

references.group: C • Philosophy and spiritual grammars
references.title: Persephone — return, divided residence, and a changed person
